why: Each paper chooses its English variant (a venue may also fix it, but IEEE accepts either when consistent); none disables the spelling check.

How the manuscript names itself in subject position, by format: this-paper in every format; this-digest (or this-letter, this-article) for that format; either = "this paper" or the name of its format (digest, letter, article), never a third name such as "this work" or "this study". IEEE Transactions house style uses this-article.

Which relative clauses are allowed (sentence.relative-clause): forbid none, nonrestrictive-only a short ", which" tail, allow both kinds; an inverted relative stays banned either way (sentence.subject-verb-adjacent).
Connectives the writing avoids (a comma word list, or none); each is flagged under sentence.no-contrast-join.
Whether hedged assertions ("might", "may") are used; strong assertions stay sparing either way.
Word count above which a sentence is flagged as too long.
Word count below which a sentence counts as very short.
Number of consecutive very short sentences that is flagged (1 flags every short sentence).
Most consecutive sentences opened by a decorative phrase plus comma.
Whether the abstract and conclusion give the key results as numbers, each after its finding ("<finding>, which is <value> in this case"), or mechanisms only.
Tense for what the paper did, in the conclusion ("This paper has analysed" or "This paper analysed").
Allowed abstract length in words, e.g. 150-250.
Style of results subsection headings (rule heading.style): declarative states the finding, topic names the subject.
Whether the venue's format is short (digest, letter, extended abstract): the introduction may then skip what the abstract already says (structure.intro-no-abstract-repeat).
Whether the introduction closes with a roadmap (introduction.roadmap): per-section gives one sentence per section stating its role; none omits it, as short formats (digest, letter) usually do.
Parts of the manuscript whose logic the author leads (a comma list such as abstract,introduction,conclusion,outline, or none): the write and review skills only propose changes to their logic.
Sentence budget of the result layer of the abstract (template abstract-layers.md); none leaves it to the word range.
Whether the conclusion closes with future work (rule conclusion.future-work); each paper decides.
